title: Air India Ordered to Reimburse Family's Rs 2.2 Lakh Singapore Shopping Bill
excerpt: A Gujarat consumer commission ruled the airline must repay Rs 1.5 lakh of emergency purchases plus Rs 1 lakh compensation after a family's luggage never left Ahmedabad in 2015.
body:
• The Gujarat State Consumer Commission has ordered Air India to reimburse Rs 1.5 lakh of a Rs 2.2 lakh emergency shopping bill run up by an Ahmedabad family whose luggage never reached Singapore.
  • The family of five, led by Dayal Wadhwani of Bhat, spent seven days in Singapore in January 2015 without their checked bags, spending 4,439 Singapore dollars on clothes and essentials.
  • The commission also awarded Rs 1 lakh compensation for deficiency in service, adding to a district commission award that had covered compensation but refused the shopping reimbursement.
  • For travellers today: file a baggage report at arrival, keep every replacement receipt — this claim succeeded on documentation pursued through two commissions.

More than a decade after an Ahmedabad family's Singapore holiday was spent without a single checked bag, Air India has been ordered to pick up most of the shopping bill the family ran up replacing what never arrived. The Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed the airline to reimburse Rs 1.5 lakh towards the family's emergency purchases, after deductions from a shopping bill of Rs 2.2 lakh, and to pay Rs 1 lakh as compensation for deficiency in service, according to reporting of the order.

Seven days, no bags

Dayal Wadhwani, a resident of Bhat, travelled to Singapore with four family members in January 2015. On arrival, the family waited in vain for their checked luggage and were told it had not been loaded onto their flight from Ahmedabad and would arrive on the next flight that evening. It never arrived during the entire seven-day trip. With their belongings missing, the family bought clothes and other essentials, spending 4,439 Singapore dollars — about Rs 2.2 lakh at the time.

Eleven years through two commissions

On returning to India, Wadhwani sent Air India a legal notice. When the airline did not respond, he approached the district Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission in Ahmedabad, which awarded Rs 1 lakh in compensation but rejected his claim for reimbursement of the shopping expenses. The state commission has now reversed that split: the Rs 1 lakh compensation stands, and Rs 1.5 lakh of the documented shopping spend is reimbursable, as NewsEdition's account of the ruling also records.

What it means for travellers

Airlines are obligated to handle passenger luggage responsibly and can be held liable for its loss under international carriage rules, including the Montreal Convention framework that governs international flights. The practical lesson of the Wadhwani case is procedural, and it is one diaspora families flying India routes can use: report the missing bag at the arrival airport before leaving, keep the baggage report reference, and retain receipts for every essential purchase — the reimbursement here was built on a documented Rs 2.2 lakh spend, and even then was trimmed to Rs 1.5 lakh. The second lesson is persistence: the full remedy took two commissions and eleven years.

The order also underlines a gap in how baggage failures are valued. The family's actual, receipted spend was Rs 2.2 lakh for five people over seven days — clothes and essentials only — yet the first commission treated that spend as unrecoverable and compensated only the distress. The state commission's split, reimbursing a trimmed Rs 1.5 lakh alongside the same Rs 1 lakh compensation, is the more complete reading of what a week without luggage actually costs a travelling family.
